title: All minors apprehended over ASEAN Summit protest released from custody
summary: All minors who were apprehended at a protest during the ASEAN Summit 2026 opening on Sunday have been released on Thursday, according to Gabriela Women's Party

blocks.text: All minors who were apprehended at a protest during the ASEAN Summit 2026 opening on Sunday have been released on Thursday, according to Gabriela Women's Party
Gabriela said in a 2 p.m. update that all of the 15 remaining minors were discharged from the facility on Thursday.
Former Gabriela Women's Party representative Arlene Brosas, lawyers, church workers, and family members were present to welcome the minors and ensure their safe release, the party said.
The release came after families and supporters repeatedly called for the minors' freedom.
Before the release, the National Union of Peoples' Lawyers (NUPL) earlier said that seven minors were still in custody as of Thursday morning.
The lawyers’ group disputed the Department of Justice's (DOJ) previous announcement that all 20 minors arrested in connection with the “Lakbayan ng Timog Katagalugan” had been released.
NUPL also welcomed the initial release of 216 protesters and journalists from Camp Bagong Diwa in Taguig City and five other minors from Bahay Pag-asa.
The Muntinlupa City Prosecutor's Office had ordered the release of the ASEAN Summit 2026 protesters from detention and custody on Wednesday.
In Manila, meanwhile, a total of nine individuals in ASEAN Summit rallies are still under police custody, according to progressive groups on Thursday. —NB, GMA News
